A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KDF/KDN research despite the changed title and extensive reorganization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V8 reports original simulations, experiments on 45 OpenML datasets, and vision experiments using ViT and ResNet-50, including appendix results.

after.justification: V9 reports original simulation, tabular, and vision results, together with network-depth and computational-scaling experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same forest and activation-path kernels, geodesic distance 1−K, nearest populated-polytope Gaussian, smoothed class counts, and additive b/log(n) term. V9's unified pseudocode, geodesic emphasis, and computation details do not establish a changed KDF/KDN procedure.

E1.justification: V8 uses CIFAR-10 as its sole vision ID benchmark. V9 additionally trains and evaluates with CIFAR-100 and SVHN as ID tasks, testing the other datasets as OOD. These are substantive new task roles for previously used OOD datasets. The six simulations and 45 OpenML datasets remain.

E2.justification: V9 adds Focal and Dual Focal to the vision comparisons in Tables 1–2. The existing Parent, Isotonic, Sigmoid, ACET, ODIN, and OE comparators remain, and the tabular comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated tabular calibration metric changes from MCE with 15 bins to ECE with 20 bins. V9 also introduces AUROC/FPR@95 evaluation and trained-versus-untrained network-depth controls, while removing the ResNet-50 configuration. The OpenML plots are retained, so the metric revision does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V9 Section 2.5 and Figure 2 newly test kernel similarity across network depths and widths, comparing same-class and different-class pairs before and after training. Appendix A and Figure 6 add polytope-count and runtime scaling analyses. The existing geodesic-versus-Euclidean, dimensionality, and image-shift analyses remain.

E5.justification: V9 specifies 10 repetitions for simulation and OpenML experiments, five seeds for vision benchmarks, and interquartile ranges for the OpenML summary. V8 reports error bars and ± values without these specifications. This is additional reporting, not evidence of increased run counts.

E6.justification: V9 adds extensive vision, detection-metric, kernel-depth, and runtime results, while v8's ResNet-50 Table 4 disappears. In the reported ViT CIFAR-10-to-SVHN comparison, KDN OCE changes from 0.08±0.02 to 0.01±0.00. V9's values for all retained methods in that row exactly match v8's ResNet-50 row; this unexplained attribution prevents treating the change as a verified same-setting gain.

T1.justification: V9 explicitly assumes equal class-conditional likelihoods in the OOD region and derives the prior-valued posterior in Equations 2–4. Its OCE definition replaces estimated priors with true priors, and Proposition 2 drops the almost-sure wording. The metric-space and asymptotic-convergence proof arguments otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: V9 describes applicability more broadly in terms of decision forests, explicitly mentioning gradient boosting trees, whereas v8 frames the forest method around random forests. The central claims of joint ID/OOD calibration without OOD training and mostly preserved classification accuracy remain.

C2.justification: The new FAQ substantially expands interpretation: calibration versus detection, distance awareness, Gaussian density versus probability mass, and baseline dependence on architecture and OOD training data. It also states concrete computational and storage limitations for very large datasets and clarifies the prior knowledge required for OCE.

D1.justification: V9 newly documents cdist-based kernel computation, the last two ViT fully connected layers, synthetic-image and noise generation, and runtime details. V8's ResNet-specific architecture and contrastive-pretraining instructions are removed. Core hyperparameter tables, hardware/software listings, and the promised future code release remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V9 substantially expands positioning around random partition kernels, spline/polytope representations, geodesic forests, and distance-aware uncertainty estimation, including Davies and Ghahramani, Black et al., and Liu et al. These connections go beyond v8's short calibration-focused related-work section. The supervised-contrastive-learning reference disappears with the ResNet study.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled Simple Calibration via Geodesic Kernels and extensively rewritten and reorganized. V9 consolidates and reorders the technical sections into Methods, moves related work into Discussion, unifies algorithm explanations, and introduces a substantial FAQ appendix. Author and publication-header text also changes.

P2.justification: V9 adds a kernel schematic, depth and runtime plots, and an OOD-detection table; expands Table 1 into ID/OOD subtables; and removes the ResNet table. V8 Figure 1 is split between v9 Figures 3 and 7, while three appendix algorithms become two main-text algorithms. Journal formatting substantially changes layout throughout.

improvement.justification: Additional ID tasks and AUROC/FPR evaluation broaden validation, while depth/scaling checks and clearer reporting make important claims easier to assess. These gains are tempered by removal of the ResNet-50 evidence and the unexplained reassignment of the SVHN OCE row, which weakens result traceability. Overall, v9 provides a limited net quality improvement.
